purpose: Replace the a003 straight rib-stick approximation with anatomically curved rib reference geometry while preserving the conventional 206-bone count.

current_a003.representation: one straight Blender segment from costovertebral region to anterior rib endpoint
current_a003.known_failure: F-RIB-001: costovertebral-to-costotransverse marker is collinear with the straight rib, so the anatomical rib-neck axis degenerates and rotation about it produces no meaningful rib motion.

anatomical_representation.bone_count_policy: Each left/right rib remains one conventional anatomical bone in the 206 inventory; curved geometry is represented by non-bone reference data/curve objects, not by inventing extra anatomical bones.
per_rib_required_data: costotransverse/tubercle contact centre for ribs 1-10 only
neck-axis vector from the true head/tubercle relationship
3D centroidal centreline from posterior head to anterior end
rib plane/best-fit plane and out-of-plane deviation
anterior endpoint/contact: costal cartilage/sternum for true ribs; costal arch for ribs 8-10; free anterior end for ribs 11-12
cross-sectional envelope samples along normalized centreline position
rib-level orientation relative to thoracic vertebra and sternum
anatomical_representation.minimum_curve_resolution: Use a parametric centreline or at least enough samples to preserve posterior curvature, lateral sweep and anterior turn; a two-point straight segment is not acceptable.

exception_policy.ribs_11_12: No costotransverse joint; do not create one. Floating-rib mechanics and endpoints must remain distinct from ribs 1-10.
exception_policy.rib_1: Morphology differs from mid-level ribs and must not be inferred solely from ribs 2-10 population models.
exception_policy.rib_12: Morphology differs from mid-level ribs and must not be inferred solely from ribs 2-11 cross-section models.

movement_implications: Pump-handle/bucket-handle motion must be generated about the actual rib-head/tubercle geometry and thoracic attachments, not an arbitrary mediolateral fallback axis.
The rib centreline and anterior contact must follow thoracic-level motion while preserving joint closure.
Rib-sternum/costal-cartilage coupling remains a separate follower/contact problem and is not solved by curve geometry alone.
acceptance_tests: Rib centreline is curved in 3D and has non-zero posterior/lateral/anterior curvature appropriate to its level.
For ribs 1-10, costovertebral and costotransverse centres are distinct and define a non-degenerate neck axis.
For ribs 11-12, no costotransverse centre exists.
Left/right rib curves are mirror-consistent within the canonical symmetry policy.
Rib-level orientation and size fall within population/stature/sex corridors after source parameter mapping.
Breathing/exercise motion uses the anatomical neck axis and preserves posterior joint contacts.
The master keeps 24 rib bones total; any extra curve points are reference data, not added bones.
next_steps: Transcribe or derive rib-level centroidal-path parameters from accessible population models.
Generate a non-deforming rib-centreline dataset for all 24 ribs.
Refit costovertebral/costotransverse/anterior contact landmarks to those curves.
Rebuild rib movement tests and remove the F-RIB-001 fallback axis only after the true neck axes exist.
